video.title: How to commit code in GitHub? 🤔 #git #github

transcript.text: Let me teach you how to commit.
I have this simple project cloned and
opened in my VS Code. Let's make some
changes now.
Notice the number here, two. This means
two files have changed. Now, let's run
Git commands to commit and push. So,
open up your terminal. The first step is
to check if you're connected to the
right repo using Git remote dash v
command.
Run Git add file name to commit a single
file or run Git add dot to push
everything.
[music]
Next, check status by running Git status
command. And if everything is okay,
commit the changes with the Git commit
command and the message version two.
Next, run Git push command. And this is
how you push code from your local
machine to GitHub. To confirm, you can
refresh the page and see that the new
commit has been made with the new
message version two. And here are your
changes.
